secondary_diagnoses: Mildly bulky bilateral kidneys (suggestive of pyelonephritis)
hospital_course: The patient presented with complaints of multiple episodes of loose stools, vomiting, fatigue, and fever. Initial evaluation revealed elevated serum creatinine (1.65mg/dl), hyponatremia (128.00mmol/L), and urinalysis showing ketone bodies, pus cells, and bacteria. The patient was treated for acute gastroenteritis, dehydration, and urinary tract infection with IV fluids, IV antibiotics, IV PPI's, and IV antiemetics. An ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis showed Grade-I fatty liver changes and features suggestive of colitis. Repeat serum creatinine was normal (1.17mg/dl). TSH and Free T4 levels were normal. The patient was discharged at the request of family for further management.
